_comment:
THE watchdog policy for every machine — desktop and VM alike. One source of truth.

WHERE THIS CAME FROM. The surface desktop's cloud-data-system-protection.json is the reference design and this is derived from it verbatim, not reinvented: it is the config that survived ten freezes and it encodes what was learned from each. The fleet inherits it and overrides only what hardware forces.

THE ONE RULE: PSI IS THE ONLY LIMITER. No absolute mem%, no RSS threshold, and above all no per-container memory.max. A hard ceiling is a LOCAL wall: the instant a cgroup touches it the kernel force-reclaims from that cgroup synchronously, however much RAM the host has free. That is not pressure management, it is thrashing on a schedule — measured on oci-apps as stalwart at 250.8MB of a 256MB cap having hit the wall 2909 times, and snappymail at 60MB of 64MB, 2852 times, while the host was fine. The desktop removed exactly these caps on 2026-08-07 for exactly this reason (see no_hard_memcap_services in the source file): plasmashell's own cap alone caused two freezes through memory.high throttle-thrash while real PSI stayed low.

WHAT REPLACES THEM. memory.high as a soft ramp (throttle, never kill), MemoryMin to protect what must stay resident, and a PSI watchdog that reads /proc/pressure and acts only when a signal actually exceeds its limit. Pressure is the thing you care about; a byte count is a proxy that is wrong whenever the host is not the bottleneck.

defaults._comment: Inherited by every profile. These are the desktop's numbers because the desktop is the reference; a profile overrides a key only where its hardware makes the desktop's answer wrong.

watchdog._comment: PSI IS THE ONLY KILL METRIC. mem/io use `full avg10` — the share of the last 10s in which ALL tasks were stalled; cpu uses `some avg10`, because a pure spin stalls some tasks and rarely all of them. Only when a signal exceeds its limit does anything get killed.

protected_slices._comment: Slices the kill path refuses to signal into, whatever signal is asked for. os-essentials is ssh/wg/session/watchdog; connectivity is the untouchable island. pid 1 is refused in code, not from this list.

reservation._comment: The untouchable island: guaranteed unreclaimable RAM, realtime CPU and IO priority, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000. The killers and the remote rescue path must be able to run when everything else is starved, or they are decorative.

memory._comment: high, never max. memory.high throttles and lets reclaim ramp; memory.max is a wall that forces synchronous reclaim the moment it is touched. Percentages of total RAM so one number serves an 8G laptop and a 1G VM.

desktop._comment: The surface. Everything here is already in defaults — this profile exists so the reference machine is named in the same table as everything that inherits from it.

specs._comment: U1 (PLAN-hardening-2026-07-07 §1C): desktop hardware specs, mirroring the vm-pilot schema _cloud-data-consolidated.json[._home_manager.vms.<vm>.specs] (ram_gb, cpu) so configuration_system-protection.nix derives its slice budgets from data instead of the old hardcoded cpus=8/ramMB=8192 let-bindings. The desktop is NOT in the cloud consolidated JSON (it is not a VM); this local desktop data file is its SoT. ram_gb×1024 = ramMB; cpu = logical CPUs (4 cores × 2 threads on the Surface Pro 8).

vm-small._comment: 1-2G, 1-2 vCPU: oci-mail, oci-analytics, gcp-proxy. On a box this size the desktop's absolute reservation is a tenth of RAM, so the island shrinks; and pressure limits come DOWN, not up — a small VM reaches genuine trouble sooner and there is less slack to ride it out.

vm-large._comment: 8G+ and container-heavy: oci-apps. Same limits as the desktop; a bigger island because there are more containers competing for the same reclaim path.

hosts._comment: Which profile each machine takes. A host absent from here gets vm-small, which is the conservative answer: tighter limits on an unknown box are recoverable, loose ones are not.
